title: Breed only the tall ones
hook: Only the tallest plants get to breed. Are their offspring as tall as they are?

knows: selection: the parents who breed pass on their genes
height depends on genes and on conditions such as soil and sun
doesNotKnow: that only the inherited share of the parents' advantage passes to offspring
the breeder's rule: response = heritability x selection

misconception: If only the tallest plants breed, the next generation averages as tall as the parents.
objective: The learner can explain that offspring of selected parents move only the inherited share of the way: kept plants 10 cm above a 100 cm field with 40% heritability give offspring of about 104 cm.

claims.text: On the stage, 40 made-up plants averaging 100 cm are kept or not by height; the tallest 15 average 110 cm.
claims.source: Heights at 40 evenly spaced quantiles of a normal curve (mean 100, spread 10) in Demo.tsx; top-15 mean 110.04 cm (artifacts/scratch/w4life/breed.mjs). No random seed. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): Node: 40 quantiles of a normal(100, 10); top 15 mean 110.04.

claims.text: With 40% of height differences inherited, offspring of parents 10 cm above average are expected to be 4 cm above average: about 104 cm. At 0% they average 100 cm; at 100%, 110 cm.
claims.source: Breeder's equation R = h2 S (Falconer & Mackay, Introduction to Quantitative Genetics, 1996, ch. 11): 0.4 x 10.04 = 4.02. Demo.tsx offMean. The brief's 400,000-plant simulation (4.6 for S = 11.6, predicted 4.64) agrees. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): Node: 100 + 0.4 x 10.04 = 104.02.

claims.text: Part of a selected parent's extra height comes from conditions such as soil and luck, which offspring do not inherit; that is why offspring move only part of the way.
claims.source: Falconer & Mackay 1996: narrow-sense heritability is the share of phenotypic variance due to additive genetic effects; the non-heritable deviations of selected parents average zero in their offspring. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): Re-derived; no issue.

claims.text: Model: made-up plants, additive genes, random crossing among the kept plants, offspring drawn with the same spread as the parents for illustration. Stated on the stage ('Toy plants') before the prediction.
claims.source: Model choice in Demo.tsx; brief life #37. The offspring spread is not modelled; only the offspring mean comes from the equation. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): Re-derived; no issue.

recall.question: Breeders cross only plants whose seeds are 20% heavier than average. 30% of seed-weight differences are inherited. The offspring's seeds will be about:
recall.why: Only the inherited share of the parents' advantage passes on: 30% of 20% is 6%.
